svg.text: "What is the max number of threads?" — there are four different ceilings
The lowest one wins. Usually it is the last one.
Framework ceiling — what YOU configure
server.tomcat.threads.max = 200 (Jetty 200, Undertow = io-threads × 8)
A hard cap you set. Raising it is one line — but see ceiling 4 before you do.
Typical sane range for a REST service: 100 – 400.
JVM memory ceiling — stack size × thread count
Each platform thread gets its own stack in NATIVE memory (not the heap). Default -Xss = 1 MB on 64-bit Linux.
max threads ≈ (RAM − heap − metaspace − code cache) / -Xss
8 GB box, -Xmx4g, ~0.5 GB other → 3.5 GB / 1 MB ≈ 3500 threads
Exceed it and you get:
OutOfMemoryError:
unable to create native thread
OS ceiling — the kernel will not give you more
ulimit -u max processes/threads per user
/proc/sys/kernel/threads-max system-wide cap (often ~100k+)
/proc/sys/vm/max_map_count each stack needs a memory mapping
In containers also check
cgroup pids.max limits.
Practical ceiling — the one that actually bites ⟵ THE REAL ANSWER
Long before memory runs out, context switching destroys you. The CPU spends its time swapping threads
instead of running them, and every downstream resource (DB pool, remote API) becomes the real bottleneck.
Realistic platform-thread limit: a few hundred, rarely useful beyond ~1000.
Going 200 → 2000 threads normally makes throughput WORSE, not better.
Virtual threads (Java 21+) remove ceilings 2, 3 and 4
They are heap objects (~a few hundred bytes), not OS threads — millions are fine. Only ceiling 1 (your config) still applies.
